annotation_scope: Matched Ensembl Plants release 63, protein-coding transcripts with CDS, one transcript per gene: prefer Ensembl_canonical; fallback longest CDS, then transcript length, then lexical transcript ID.
point_definition: midpoint0 = (start0 + end0 - 1) / 2; a 1024-bp window has midpoint start0+511.5 in 0-based base coordinates.
coordinate_system: GTF 1-based closed features converted to 0-based half-open intervals; point containment start0 <= midpoint0 < end0.
flank_definition: Intervals are relative to canonical transcript boundaries and genomic strand. + strand: upstream [txStart-1000,txStart), [txStart-3000,txStart-1000), downstream [txEnd,txEnd+1000). - strand reverses direction: upstream [txEnd,txEnd+1000), [txEnd+1000,txEnd+3000), downstream [txStart-1000,txStart). Chromosome edges clipped.
CDS_definition: Annotated canonical CDS plus annotated start_codon and stop_codon, so the coding region includes its stop codon.
intron_definition: Gaps strictly between successive merged canonical transcript exons; residual exon segments are never treated as introns.
distal_definition: Outside the eight reference categories relative to selected canonical protein-coding transcripts; this is not equivalent to intergenic relative to all annotated noncoding genes.
overlap_resolution: Gene-body features take priority over nearby-gene flanks; listed global feature priority resolves overlaps. Both predicted strands use the same region assignment.
unclassified_exon_rule: Any canonical coding-transcript exon segments outside annotated CDS/start/stop/5UTR/3UTR remain an explicit unclassified_coding_exon audit category, never forced into CDS/intron/distal.
statistics: Pearson r main figure and Spearman rho supplemental table; both calculated from all windows within each region on x=log2(1+mean SRX CPM), y=log2(1+raw predicted score). n<3 or constant inputs produce NA.
error_bars: None: one frozen model per species and no independent biological/model replicates of each coefficient. Test windows are not treated as biological replicates.
